newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court gives standing to rejected bidder in PHARE program.
newsitem.headline: Court gives standing to rejected bidder in PHARE program.

text.p: The European Court of Justice annuled on Tuesday a judgment from the Court of First Instance which denied Geotronics SA a right of appeal against the European Commission.

Although the substance of the earlier ruling was upheld and the court confirmed the dismissal of damage claims against the Commission, it did take a fresh look at whether companies denied contracts under the PHARE program have standing to challenge the Commission's decision-making.

The general rule is that measures adopted by Commission representatives concerning the award of public contracts are intended solely to establish whether bidding criteria have been met, and these measures are not actionable, the court said.

However, the court found in this case that the Commission decision not to accept Geotronics' bid, which was formally addressed to Geotronics, was taken after it had ascertained whether Geotronics' tender satisfied the conditions for obtianing Community funding.

"In those circumstances, the Commission's decision to refuse Geotronics the benefit of Community funding in itself had binding legal effect as regards the appellant and could therefore be the subject of an action for annulment," the court said.
